title: Exploratory Analysis of Colorectal Cancer (CRC) Microbial Signatures
text: Requiring least three independent studies least 75% directional agreement common, interpretable threshold calling taxon “core”: rules one-findings still tolerating disagreement studies differ cohort, region, platform.
code: concordance <- taxon.long %>%   distinct(PMID, taxon, direction) %>%   group_by(taxon) %>%   summarise(     n_studies       = n_distinct(PMID),     n_increased     = sum(direction == "increased"),     n_decreased     = sum(direction == "decreased"),     concordance_pct = round(max(n_increased, n_decreased) / n_studies * 100, 1),     majority_dir    = if_else(n_increased >= n_decreased, "increased", "decreased"),     .groups = "drop"   ) %>%   arrange(desc(n_studies), desc(concordance_pct))  # Formal threshold for a "core" signature: reported in at least 3 independent # studies, with at least 75% of those studies agreeing on direction core.sig <- concordance %>%   filter(n_studies >= 3, concordance_pct >= 75) %>%   arrange(majority_dir, desc(n_studies))  nrow(core.sig) ## [1] 102 knitr::kable(core.sig) core.sig %>%   mutate(     direction_label = if_else(majority_dir == "increased",                                "Increased in CRC", "Decreased in CRC"),     # Wrap long taxon names onto a second line instead of letting them     # overlap or run off the plot area     taxon_label = paste0(str_wrap(taxon, width = 28), " (", n_studies, ")")   ) %>%   ggplot(aes(x = reorder(taxon_label, n_studies), y = n_studies, fill = direction_label)) +   geom_col(width = 0.7) +   geom_text(aes(label = paste0(concordance_pct, "%")), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.3) +   coord_flip(clip = "off") +   facet_wrap(~direction_label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +   scale_fill_manual(values = c("Increased in CRC" = "#B22222",                                 "Decreased in CRC" = "#006400")) +   # Extra headroom on the right so the "%" labels never get clipped   scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.35))) +   labs(     title = "Core CRC Consensus Signature",     subtitle = "Taxa in >=3 studies with >=75% direction concordance",     x = NULL, y = "Number of independent studies", fill = NULL   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   theme(     legend.position = "none",     plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),     axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, lineheight = 0.9),     strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),     plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 20, b = 10, l = 10)   )

title: Exploratory Analysis of Colorectal Cancer (CRC) Microbial Signatures
text: binomial test compares taxon’s observed frequency frequency expected taxa reported random full pool fecal CRC taxa. Taxa small adjusted p-value reported far often chance predict, independent core-signature concordance threshold .
code: n.universe <- n_distinct(taxon.long$taxon) n.sigs     <- length(sigs.feces)  enrichment.df <- taxon.freq %>%   distinct(taxon, total_studies) %>%   mutate(     observed         = total_studies,     expected         = n.sigs / n.universe,     enrichment_ratio = observed / expected,     log2_enrichment  = log2(enrichment_ratio),     p_value = purrr::map_dbl(observed, ~ binom.test(       x = .x, n = n.sigs, p = 1 / n.universe, alternative = "greater"     )$p.value),     p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")   ) %>%   arrange(p_adj, desc(log2_enrichment))  sum(enrichment.df$p_adj < 0.05) ## [1] 167 knitr::kable(head(enrichment.df, 15))

title: Exploratory Analysis of Colorectal Cancer (CRC) Microbial Signatures
text: Co-occurrence identifies taxa tend reported together within study, suggestive shared microbial community shift. Co-exclusion identifies taxa reported opposite directions within study, may point competitive antagonistic relationships taxa CRC gut environment.
code: top.taxa <- taxon.freq %>%   distinct(taxon, total_studies) %>%   slice_max(total_studies, n = 30) %>%   pull(taxon)  presence.mat <- taxon.long %>%   filter(taxon %in% top.taxa) %>%   distinct(PMID, taxon) %>%   mutate(present = 1L) %>%   pivot_wider(names_from = taxon, values_from = present, values_fill = 0L) %>%   column_to_rownames("PMID") %>%   as.matrix()  co.occ.mat <- t(presence.mat) %*% presence.mat diag(co.occ.mat) <- 0  co.occ.pairs <- which(upper.tri(co.occ.mat), arr.ind = TRUE) %>%   as.data.frame() %>%   mutate(     taxon_a   = rownames(co.occ.mat)[row],     taxon_b   = colnames(co.occ.mat)[col],     n_studies = co.occ.mat[cbind(row, col)]   ) %>%   filter(n_studies > 0) %>%   arrange(desc(n_studies)) %>%   slice_max(n_studies, n = 15)  knitr::kable(co.occ.pairs %>% select(taxon_a, taxon_b, n_studies)) co.excl <- taxon.long %>%   filter(taxon %in% top.taxa) %>%   distinct(PMID, taxon, direction) %>%   inner_join(     taxon.long %>% filter(taxon %in% top.taxa) %>% distinct(PMID, taxon, direction),     by = "PMID", suffix = c("_a", "_b"), relationship = "many-to-many"   ) %>%   filter(taxon_a < taxon_b, direction_a != direction_b) %>%   count(taxon_a, taxon_b, name = "n_coexclusion") %>%   filter(n_coexclusion >= 2) %>%   arrange(desc(n_coexclusion))  nrow(co.excl) ## [1] 208 knitr::kable(head(co.excl, 15))

title: Exploratory Analysis of Colorectal Cancer (CRC) Microbial Signatures
text: Comparing CRC taxon set related diseases (IBD, obesity, NAFLD, adenoma) gives sense specificity: “core” CRC signature overlaps heavily several unrelated conditions likely reflect general gut dysbiosis disease-specific mechanism. Note: comparison.conditions strings checked unique(dat$Condition) session, since exact BugSigDB condition labels can differ slightly common usage.
code: comparison.conditions <- c(   "Crohn's disease", "Ulcerative colitis", "Inflammatory Bowel Diseases",   "Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease", "Obesity", "Colorectal adenoma" )  other.diseases <- dat %>% filter(Condition %in% comparison.conditions)  disease.taxa <- purrr::map_dfr(comparison.conditions, function(cond) {   sub.df <- other.diseases %>% filter(Condition == cond)   if (nrow(sub.df) == 0) return(NULL)   sigs.sub <- bugsigdbr::getSignatures(sub.df, tax.id.type = "taxname")   tibble::tibble(taxon = unique(unlist(sigs.sub)), condition = cond) })  crc.taxa.set <- unique(unlist(sigs.feces))  overlap.summary <- purrr::map_dfr(comparison.conditions, function(cond) {   other.set <- disease.taxa %>% filter(condition == cond) %>% pull(taxon)   if (length(other.set) == 0) return(NULL)   tibble::tibble(     condition          = cond,     n_taxa_other       = length(other.set),     n_shared_with_crc  = length(intersect(crc.taxa.set, other.set)),     jaccard            = round(length(intersect(crc.taxa.set, other.set)) /                                   length(union(crc.taxa.set, other.set)), 3)   ) })  knitr::kable(overlap.summary)

title: Exploratory Analysis of Colorectal Cancer (CRC) Microbial Signatures
text: exploratory analysis identified 192 fecal, human-derived colorectal cancer microbial signatures curated BugSigDB. Beyond taxonomic summary, Monte Carlo critical-N estimation, pairwise Jaccard similarity/heatmap/dendrogram analyses, several additional layers evidence used characterize candidate “core” CRC-associated signature: formal core-signature threshold (≥3 independent studies, ≥75% directional concordance) narrowed taxon list 102 taxa consistent evidence. WMS vs 16S concordance checked whether consistency holds across sequencing platforms, flagging taxa whose direction may platform-dependent rather biological. Binomial enrichment testing identified taxa reported far often chance, independent concordance threshold. Co-occurrence co-exclusion analyses added network view taxa move together opposition within studies. Cross-disease overlap IBD, obesity, NAFLD, adenoma assessed specific CRC signature CRC versus general gut dysbiosis. Geographic temporal trends checked whether evidence base dominated single region era. diagnostic-relevance check known oncomicrobiome markers (e.g. Fusobacterium nucleatum, Parvimonas micra) provided lightweight sanity check whether database-derived signature recovers established biology. Together, results provide multi-angle starting point identifying candidate core CRC-associated gut microbial signature prioritizing taxa validation, rather relying single metric isolation.

code: allsigs <- bugsigdbr::getSignatures(   masld.filtered,   tax.id.type = "taxname" )  # Keep signatures containing at least two taxa allsigs <- allsigs[sapply(allsigs, length) > 1]  length(allsigs) ## [1] 39 # Pairwise overlaps mydists <- BugSigDBStats::calcPairwiseOverlaps(allsigs)  dim(mydists) ## [1] 144   8 # Jaccard similarity matrix jmat <- BugSigDBStats::calcJaccardSimilarity(allsigs)  # Keep BugSigDB study/experiment identifiers row_labels <- sub("^bsdb:", "PMID", sub("_.*$", "", rownames(jmat))) col_labels <- sub("^bsdb:", "PMID", sub("_.*$", "", colnames(jmat)))

title: Exploratory Analysis of MASLD Microbial Signatures
text: heatmap visualizes pairwise Jaccard similarities among MASLD-associated microbial signatures, highlighting groups studies similar taxonomic compositions.
code: library(grid) library(ComplexHeatmap)  # Calculate signature lengths siglengths <- sapply(allsigs, length)  # Short labels for display short.labels <- paste0("S", seq_len(nrow(jmat)))  # Top annotation ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(   `Signature\nLength` = anno_barplot(     siglengths,     gp = gpar(fill = 4:(length(siglengths) + 3)),     annotation_name_gp = gpar(       fontsize = 10,       lineheight = 0.8     )   ) )  # Left annotation hr <- rowAnnotation(   `Signature\nLength` = anno_barplot(     siglengths,     gp = gpar(fill = 4:(length(siglengths) + 3)),     annotation_name_gp = gpar(       fontsize = 10,       lineheight = 0.8     )   ) )  # Create heatmap hm <- Heatmap(   jmat,    top_annotation = ha,   left_annotation = hr,    row_names_max_width = unit(10, "cm"),   column_names_max_height = unit(3, "cm"),    row_labels = row_labels,   column_labels = col_labels,    row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8),   column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8),    column_title = "Heatmap of Similarity of MASLD Microbial Signatures",   column_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 15),    heatmap_legend_param = list(     title = "Jaccard Similarity",     direction = "horizontal"   ) )  # Draw heatmap draw(   hm,   heatmap_legend_side = "bottom",   annotation_legend_side = "right" ) # Save the heatmap as a high-resolution PNG png(   filename = file.path(tempdir(), "MASLD_heatmap.png"),   width = 14,   height = 10,   units = "in",   res = 300 )  draw(   hm,   heatmap_legend_side = "bottom",   annotation_legend_side = "right" )  dev.off() ## agg_png  ##       2
